rows.text: Sisay's power counts COLOURS among your other legendary permanents, not how many you control — so a single five-colour board makes her a 7/7 that tutors any legendary permanent costing six or less directly onto the battlefield. Each fetch adds colours, which grows her, which raises the ceiling on the next fetch. The whole deck is about paying for the first activation; after that it snowballs.

rows.name: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain
rows.text: base 2/2, +1/+1 per colour among your OTHER legendary permanents, and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} searches out a legendary permanent with mana value strictly LESS than her power, straight onto the battlefield. Count before you activate.

rows.name: Esika, God of the Tree
rows.text: taps for any colour AND gives every other legendary creature "{T}: add one mana of any colour". With three legends out, that alone pays Sisay's activation.

rows.name: Faeburrow Elder
rows.text: taps for one mana of each colour among your permanents. On a five-colour board it is a one-card Sisay activation.

rows.name: Jegantha, the Wellspring
rows.text: taps for exactly {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}. It is not a legal companion for this deck — Flowering of the White Tree and Mana Drain both break the rule — so it lives in the ninety-nine as the cleanest enabler you have.

rows.name: Ioreth of the Healing House
rows.text: untaps two other legendary creatures. Untap Faeburrow Elder and Jegantha and Sisay activates twice in a turn.

rows.name: Relic of Legends
rows.text: taps for any colour, and taps a legendary creature for another.

rows.name: Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy
rows.text: doubles every nonland mana source you tap, which turns Faeburrow Elder or Esika into two activations.

rows.name: Mox Amber
rows.text: free, and live from turn one in a deck this legendary.

rows.name: Delighted Halfling
rows.text: uncounterable mana for legendary spells, which is nearly your whole deck.

rows.name: Bloom Tender
rows.text: two or three colours off one tap early.

rows.name: Loki's Scepter
rows.text: fixes, and steals a creature for a turn on the way in.
Fetch to fix your colours first. The correct first activation is almost always the legend that adds a missing colour — that raises Sisay's power and makes the NEXT fetch bigger.

rows.name: Jodah, the Unifier
rows.text: your legends all get +X/+X for your legend count, and every legendary spell you cast from hand cascades into a cheaper legend for free.

rows.name: Kethis, the Hidden Hand

rows.name: Lavinia, Azorius Renegade
rows.text: the fetch against a combo table. Nothing cast for free resolves, and their expensive noncreature spells stop working.

rows.name: Jennifer Walters

rows.name: Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar

rows.name: Reki, the History of Kamigawa
rows.text: a card for every legendary spell you cast, which is most of them.

rows.name: Jhoira, Weatherlight Captain

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep fixing over threats. Five specific colours is the deck's entire difficulty — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Arcane Signet and Delighted Halfling matter more than any single legend.

Count Sisay's power BEFORE you tap out. Five colours among your other legendary permanents makes her a 7/7, which fetches mana value six. Four colours caps you at five. Adding a colour is often worth more than adding a bomb.

rows.name: Esika, God of the Tree
rows.text: this is the fetch that unlocks everything else. She fixes, she ramps, and every legend you already control starts tapping for mana the moment she resolves.

rows.name: Jodah, the Unifier
rows.text: cast your legends FROM HAND while he is out. Each one cascades into a free legend, and this deck's curve means the free hits are real cards.
